emergency.notes: Emergency services can be slow outside Phnom Penh. English-speaking operators rare — hotel staff can assist. Tourist Police: +855-23-724-793.

travelAdvisory.summary: Exercise increased caution in Cambodia due to crime, civil unrest, and unexploded ordnance (UXO) in rural areas. Land mines remain a risk in remote areas near the Thai border.

travelAdvisoryUK.summary: Most visits to Cambodia are trouble-free. Be alert to petty theft and bag snatching. Avoid walking alone at night in cities. Exercise caution in areas with unexploded ordnance.

healthcare.systemType: Underdeveloped public system; private hospitals in Phnom Penh and Siem Reap recommended for tourists
healthcare.costForTourists: Private clinic visit $30-80. Emergency care at international clinics $100-400. Serious conditions require evacuation to Bangkok (approx. $15,000-50,000). Hospital stay at private facilities $200-600/night.
healthcare.pharmacyAccess: Pharmacies common in cities. Quality varies — counterfeit medications exist. Stick to reputable pharmacies in tourist areas.
healthcare.hospitalNotes: Calmette Hospital and Royal Phnom Penh Hospital serve emergencies. For serious conditions, medical evacuation to Bangkok or Singapore is strongly recommended.
healthcare.insuranceAdvice: Comprehensive travel insurance including emergency medical evacuation is essential. Medical facilities outside Phnom Penh are severely limited.

pharmacy.hours: Pharmacies are widely available in Phnom Penh and Siem Reap, typically open 8am-9pm. Rural areas have fewer pharmacies with limited stock. Look for 'Pharmacy' or 'Store' signs — many medications are sold in general stores.
pharmacy.tips: Many medications available by prescription in Western countries are available OTC in Cambodia. Antibiotics, pain medications, and other drugs can often be purchased without prescription. Quality of medications varies — counterfeits are a known problem. Stick to reputable pharmacies in cities.

vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for most travelers. However, Hepatitis A, Hepatitis B, Typhoid, and Rabies are strongly recommended due to variable healthcare and food/water safety. Ensure routine vaccinations are current. Consider Japanese Encephalitis vaccination for extended rural stays.

water.notes: Do NOT drink tap water in Cambodia. Bottled water is essential — always drink sealed bottled water. Use bottled or purified water for brushing teeth. Avoid ice in drinks outside reputable establishments.

healthcare.foodSafetyTips: Be very cautious with food. Eat at reputable restaurants. Avoid raw vegetables and salads unless you're confident in the establishment. Peel fruits yourself. Only eat cooked foods served hot. Street food can be risky — only eat from busy, clean-looking stalls. Diarrhea is very common.

travelInsurance.requiredNote: Strongly recommended, and some travel insurance is required for visa-on-arrival for some nationalities. Make sure your insurance covers medical evacuation — critical for serious conditions.
travelInsurance.tips: Medical evacuation to Bangkok costs $10,000-30,000+. This is the single most important coverage. Public hospitals are inadequate for serious conditions. Private clinics are better but still limited. Carry your insurance contact numbers. Phnom Penh has some good private hospitals but serious conditions need evacuation.

healthcare.qualityNotes: Healthcare quality varies dramatically. Phnom Penh and Siem Reap have international clinics with decent care (Royal Phnom Penh Hospital, Sunrise Japan Hospital, Angkor Hospital for Children). Rural areas have very limited facilities. Serious medical conditions require evacuation to Bangkok or Singapore. English is commonly spoken in tourist-oriented medical facilities.

commonOTC: antimalarial medication (limited availability — bring your own)
medications.prescriptionRules: Prescription requirements are not strictly enforced. However, carrying your prescription and doctor's letter is recommended. For controlled substances, a Cambodian doctor may need to re-prescribe. Counterfeit medications are a serious concern — use reputable pharmacies.

restrictedMeds.name: Diazepam (Valium) and benzodiazepines
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled. Requires prescription. Carry your foreign prescription and doctor's letter. Quantities for personal use are permitted with documentation.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled. Some codeine products may be available OTC. Bring your prescription and doctor's letter.

restrictedMeds.name: Tramadol
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled opioid. Requires prescription. Bring your documentation.

restrictedMeds.name: ADHD medications (Adderall, Ritalin, Vyvanse)
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled. Requires documentation and possibly Cambodian doctor consultation. Contact your embassy for guidance.

restrictedMeds.name: Medical cannabis
restrictedMeds.note: Cannabis is illegal in Cambodia. Despite some leniency toward small amounts for personal use in practice, it remains illegal. Do not bring cannabis products.

medications.bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in English listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. Bring all medications you might need — supply chains are unreliable. For any serious condition, bring a complete supply for your trip plus extra.

connectivity.simOptions: Tourist SIMs from Cellcard, Smart, or Metfone available at airports and markets for $2-10. Data packages are cheap: 5GB for ~$3. eSIM via Airalo.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Good free WiFi in hotels, cafes, and restaurants in cities. Limited in rural areas and small towns.
connectivity.bestOption: Cellcard or Smart SIM for best coverage. Buy at airport arrivals or convenience stores.

cultural.tipping: Not customary traditionally but appreciated in tourist areas. Restaurants: $1-2 or 10%. Tuk-tuk drivers: round up. Temple guides: $2-5. Hotel staff: $1-2/bag.
cultural.dressCode: Dress modestly at temples — cover shoulders and knees. Remove shoes before entering temples. Light, breathable clothing suitable for tropical heat.
cultural.greetings: Traditional greeting is the 'Sampeah' — press palms together in prayer position and bow slightly. Say 'Chhom reap suor' (formal) or 'Susaday' (informal). Do not touch heads — considered sacred.
taboos: Pointing feet at people or sacred objects
Wearing shoes inside temples and some homes
Disrespecting the king or royal family (can result in arrest)
cultural.haggling: Expected and normal at markets. Start at 50% of asking price. Fixed prices in proper shops and restaurants.

safety.lgbtSafety: Same-sex relationships are not criminalized but LGBTQ+ rights are limited. Public displays of affection by same-sex couples may attract negative attention in conservative areas.
safety.soloFemaleSafety: Exercise caution, especially at night. Avoid walking alone after dark in cities. Bag snatching from motorbikes is common. Dress modestly to reduce unwanted attention.
safety.notes: Main risks are petty theft, bag snatching from motorbikes, and scams targeting tourists. UXO risk in rural northwest areas near Thai border. Avoid random invitations from strangers which may lead to scams.

practical.visaFreeCountries: Most nationalities require a visa. E-visa available online. 30-day tourist visa on arrival available for many countries for $30.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: November to March (dry season, cooler temperatures 25-35°C). Avoid May-October (monsoon with heavy flooding). Angkor Wat sunrise is spectacular year-round.

hospitals.name: Royal Phnom Penh Hospital
hospitals.notes: Best private hospital in Phnom Penh. English-speaking staff and international-standard care.

hospitals.name: Calmette Hospital
hospitals.notes: Main government hospital. Limited English. Best for stabilization before transfer.

hospitals.name: Royal Angkor International Hospital
hospitals.notes: Best hospital near Angkor Wat temples. Good English-speaking staff.

immediate: Move to higher ground immediately — do not attempt to walk through floodwaters
Avoid roads during flash floods — depth is deceptive and currents are strong
Do not touch electrical equipment near standing water
Follow instructions from local authorities and hotel staff
after: Avoid contact with floodwater which may be contaminated
Check road conditions before traveling — many rural roads become impassable
Monitor local radio and government alerts for flooding updates
resources: National Committee for Disaster Management (NCDM): www.ncdm.gov.kh

immediate: Never stray off marked paths in rural areas, especially near Thai border
If you see a suspicious metal object, do not touch or move it
Mark the location and inform local authorities
Evacuate the immediate area and keep others away
after: Report any UXO find to CMAC (Cambodia Mine Action Centre)
Do not return to area until cleared by authorities
